references.text: The Lord's judgment on Israel's rebellious generation, who had to wander in the wilderness for forty years until all the warriors who came out of Egypt were dead because they did not obey the Lord's voice.
The Lord's anger toward Israel, which led them to wander in the wilderness for forty years until the entire generation that had done what was evil in the Lord's sight was gone.
The Lord's oath that none of that wicked generation would see the good land he had sworn to give their fathers.
The thirty-eight years Israel wandered from Kadesh-barnea until they crossed the Zered Brook, until the entire generation of warriors had disappeared from the camp, as the Lord had sworn.
The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey, given to the fathers.
The description of the promised land as a land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord's oath that those who despised him would not see the land he had sworn to give their fathers.
The psalm that recalls the forty years when the Lord was angry with the wilderness generation and swore they would not enter his rest.
Hebrews' reminder that it was those who sinned and disobeyed who fell in the wilderness and could not enter the rest because of unbelief.
